title: An in-flight reconnect can undo an explicit Leave Room
test: tests/browser/media-flow.spec.mjs: 'Leave Room pressed while a reconnect is rejoining the room stays left, starts no playback and leaves no viewer behind' and 'a rejoin left behind by Leave Room finishes without undoing the join made after it' (chromium); tests/viewerSession.test.js: 'a session is current until something ends it or a newer one begins', 'a join completion whose session is behind the current one is rejected, and commits nothing', 'a join that finishes while its session is current commits and sends no leave', 'every await of a join is followed by a check: the session can end at any of them', 'the compensating leave is sent only when no newer join has begun since the session ended', 'a join the server refused, or that never left, has nothing to undo', 'a join that fails while its session is current reports its own error', 'a view that unmounted sends no leave: the socket may belong to another view now', 'a leave that throws because the socket went away does not hide the stale join', 'WatchView ends the session before Leave Room waits for the server, and commits a join only after a check'
proof: Browser repro 1: a viewer watching over WebRTC has its Socket.IO WebSocket dropped; an init-script WebSocket subclass holds back the reconnect's outgoing join-room frame (a slow network; the rejoin is then in flight while the joined view, Leave Room included, stays usable). Leave Room is pressed: the join form appears and the server has no viewer. The held join-room is then released: the server (which handled leave-room first) puts the viewer back in the room and answers the rejoin. On the unchanged code (lane/watch 80da94f, run-e2e.cjs on the lane's own ports; scratchpad watch-TASK-090-before-e2e-final.txt) the test failed at 'the client asks the server to drop that viewer again': the frames sent after the release were join-room, get-rtp-capabilities, create-recv-transport, get-producers, consume, connect-transport, consumer-resume. The stale join committed its state and the reconnect resumed WebRTC playback in a room the viewer had left, with no leave-room. The second test (Leave, then Join again while the old join-room is still held) failed on the unchanged code earlier: after Join the page showed a disabled 'Connecting...' button next to Leave Room, because handleLeave never cleared the loading state the reconnect had set and the old rejoin's finally had not run yet. After the fix: both pass, 3 of 3 with --repeat-each=3; test 1 sees one compensating leave-room, viewerCount 0 at the server, the join form, no alert, no mode text and none of get-rtp-capabilities, create-recv-transport, consume, relay-consume-start, fallback-consume-start after the release; test 2 sees the old rejoin send nothing more, the newer join untouched (viewerCount 1, Leave Room and an enabled Watch Stream) and Watch Stream then playing over WebRTC. Fix: src/lib/viewerSession.mjs holds a generation (begin on a join, invalidate when a session ends, close on unmount); joinRoomAndLoadDevice takes a session token and checks it after join-room, get-rtp-capabilities, getDevice and device.load, and the only setJoined(true) comes after the last check with no await between; a stale join commits nothing, resets the device module's singleton (unless a newer join uses it) and throws StaleViewerSessionError after abandonStaleJoin sent the compensating leave-room (section-49e0545c60d121dd3e784d86/Q-003: only if the join-room was not refused, no newer join began since the session ended, and the view is still mounted). handleLeave invalidates before its first await, clears a queued recovery and the loading state; the terminal transport-failed branch, room-ended and the unmount cleanup end the session too; handleJoin begins its session after the joiningRef guard; the reconnect rejoin begins its own session, does not start while the session has ended (Leave Room waiting for its answer), returns without resuming playback, without the relay fallback and without the reset-to-unjoined branch when its session is stale, and leaves the loading state to whoever ended the session. The unit tests drive the same helper (a join harness with the shape of joinRoomAndLoadDevice) and check WatchView's source: the unit file's helper tests could not run before (new module); its source guard failed on the unchanged WatchView ('handleLeave ends the session', watch-TASK-090-before-unit.txt). Verification: whole media-flow spec 23/23 (watch-TASK-090-after-media-flow.txt), ui-semantics.spec.mjs 93/93, node --test tests/viewerSession.test.js 10/10; npm run lint and typecheck clean; npm test 1484/1484.
